Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:

– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test org.apache.commons.math.stat.FrequencyTest.testAddNonComparable() expects that calling f.addValue(new Object()) throws an IllegalArgumentException immediately.

Inspecting the implementation:

- Frequency.addValue(Object) (lines 108–110):
  - The method simply casts the argument to Comparable<?> and delegates:
    - addValue((Comparable<?>) v);
  - If v is a plain Object (not Comparable), this cast itself throws a ClassCastException before any further logic runs.

- Frequency.addValue(Comparable<?>) (lines 123–139):
  - This method inserts into a raw TreeMap (freqTable).
  - It wraps TreeMap’s potential ClassCastException (thrown when comparing non-mutually-comparable keys) and rethrows it as an IllegalArgumentException: "Value not comparable to existing values."

- Frequency constructors (lines 57–68):
  - freqTable is a raw TreeMap; inserting the first non-comparable key into an empty TreeMap would normally succeed, and a failure would occur on a subsequent add when a comparison is required—matching the issue report’s previous behavior.

How the bug manifests with the current code:
- The deprecated addValue(Object) performs an unchecked cast to Comparable<?>. When given a non-Comparable (e.g., new Object()), it fails with a ClassCastException at the cast site, not with the intended IllegalArgumentException. The test catches only IllegalArgumentException and therefore fails.

Why this contradicts the intended behavior:
- The API should not accept non-Comparable objects. Per the bug report and test, attempting to add a plain Object should result in an IllegalArgumentException. The Comparable overload already maps TreeMap’s ClassCastException to IllegalArgumentException for comparability issues, but addValue(Object) never gets there because it fails earlier at the cast.

Root cause:
- Frequency.addValue(Object) incorrectly casts to Comparable without checking, causing a ClassCastException to escape instead of the expected IllegalArgumentException for non-Comparable inputs.

In short: addValue(Object) should validate the argument (instanceof Comparable) and throw IllegalArgumentException if not comparable, instead of performing a blind cast that raises ClassCastException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
